name: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat
alternative_names: Smith Machine Rear-Foot Elevated Split Squat
description: The Smith machine Bulgarian split squat replicates the standard dumbbell or barbell Bulgarian split squat using the guided bar of the Smith machine. The fixed bar path reduces the balance demands and allows the lifter to focus on depth and muscular feel rather than stability. The rear foot is elevated on a bench behind, and the front leg does the primary work.

execution.starting_position: Set the Smith machine bar at shoulder height. Position a bench behind you. Place one foot on the bench (top of foot or heel, depending on comfort). Position the front foot forward so the front shin will be vertical at the bottom.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the Smith machine bar to sit across the traps. Place a flat or adjustable bench 2-3 feet behind the machine's path. Set rear foot on bench before unracking.
steps: Step 1: Brace the core and keep an upright torso.
Step 2: Lower the rear knee directly down toward the floor.
Step 3: Descend until the front thigh is at or below parallel. Front shin should remain nearly vertical.
Step 4: Drive through the front heel to extend back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent, exhale on the drive.
common_mistakes: Front foot too close, causing excessive forward shin angle
Rear knee drifting to one side
Leaning the torso too far forward
safety_considerations: The rear foot on the bench creates instability — set up carefully and test before loading
The Smith machine's fixed path may feel unnatural for some — adjust foot position accordingly
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Front thigh at or below parallel. Rear knee close to floor.
coaching_cues: Drive the rear knee straight down
